cards.text: John, the servant God gave this vision to (Rev 1:1), just heard a sound like the roar of a great multitude: the marriage of the Lamb has come, and the bride was given "clothing of fine linen, bright and pure" (Rev 19:6-8). Then John looks up, and heaven is standing open, and there before him is a white horse with a rider.

cards.question: The rider on the white horse has a name. What is He called?

cards.text: Faithful and True, friend, and I shared a junk drawer with dead batteries that swore they still had a charge, so I KNOW how rare that is! John says this rider does two things: He judges, and He wages war.

cards.question: The rider called Faithful and True judges and wages war with ___.

cards.text: The rider has eyes like blazing fire and many royal crowns on His head, and friend, I wear ONE tall white hat and I still bump it on the oven hood. And there's a name written on Him.

cards.question: The name written on the rider is one that everyone around Him knows.

cards.text: Nope, only He Himself knows that name. He's dressed in a robe dipped in blood, and John has another name for Him, one John CAN tell us.

cards.question: John says the rider's name is The Word of God.

cards.text: Then the armies of heaven ride out behind Him on white horses. Friend, the only thing that ever followed ME anywhere was a trail of flour.

cards.question: What are the armies of heaven following the rider dressed in?

cards.text: Fine linen, white and pure. And then something proceeds from the rider's mouth.

cards.question: Something proceeds from the rider's mouth to strike down the nations. It's a sharp ___.

cards.text: A sharp sword. He will rule the nations with an iron scepter, and John says He treads a winepress, the kind you stomp, and this one is full of fury.

cards.question: The rider treads the winepress of the fury of someone's wrath. Whose wrath is it?

cards.text: One more name, and this one is written right on His robe and on His thigh. Me, I've got Dorin carved on my handle, and friend, most days you can't read it through the flour.

cards.question: The rider wears many royal crowns. What name is written on His robe and on His thigh?

answers.text: KING OF KINGS AND LORD OF LORDS
HOLY HOLY HOLY LORD GOD ALMIGHTY
MIGHTY GOD AND PRINCE OF PEACE

cards.text: Then John sees an angel standing in the sun, crying out in a loud voice. Standing in the SUN, friend, and I break a sweat just opening my oven door.

cards.question: The angel standing in the sun cries out in a loud voice. Who is he calling?

cards.text: The birds, and he tells them to come and gather together for the great supper of God. Friend, I heard SUPPER and grabbed my apron, but look at that guest list, because that is NOT the supper I'm baking for.

cards.question: The angel tells the birds whose flesh they will eat, and his list covers only the powerful, like kings and commanders.

cards.text: Not even close: kings, horses, riders, everyone slave and free, small and great. Then John sees the beast, the one he saw rising out of the sea (Rev 13:1), and the kings of the earth with their armies, assembled to wage war against the One on the horse and His army.

cards.question: The beast and the kings of the earth line up their armies against the rider, and the beast gets away.

cards.text: Nope, the beast is captured, along with the false prophet, the one who acted on its behalf. John doesn't even describe a fight, and friend, I've had longer battles with a jar lid.

cards.question: The false prophet acted on the beast's behalf. What did he do?

answers.text: Wrote new laws for the kings

cards.question: The beast and the false prophet are both thrown somewhere, alive. Where?

answers.text: The fiery lake of burning sulfur

cards.text: The fiery lake of burning sulfur. As for the rest of them, the kings and their armies, John tells us how their end comes.

cards.question: The rest of the beast's side are killed with the ___ that proceeded from the rider's mouth.

cards.text: The sword that proceeded from His mouth. And all those birds the angel called come and gorge themselves, just like the angel said.

findings.problem: The opening introduces John and the vision but never says to whom John is speaking or writing. It gives what is happening without identifying the passage's audience.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: Discovery guesses recur too often across both stops. The setups for stop 1 cards 2, 6, 8 and 12 and stop 2 cards 2 and 9 provide no basis for reasoning out Faithful and True, the name's secrecy, The Word of God, the sword, the birds or the fiery lake. The clothing question in stop 1 card 10 and the guest-list question in stop 2 card 4 likewise depend on details not established by their setups. Rather than a few discovery moments, luck becomes a substantial part of the walkthrough.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer. The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question. A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.
